headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading error concerns: Chatwoot handles customer data with broad egress while awesome-prompts is an unverified prompt source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository, so its outputs can plausibly be copied into Chatwoot workflows. Chatwoot has customer-support integrations and broad egress, making prompt-injection via pasted content or shared artifacts plausible, though no shared channel is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF outputs from awesome-prompts are pasted into Chatwoot tickets or macros
IF Chatwoot operators treat imported prompt text as instructions
mitigations: Restrict pasted prompt content to a review-only queue
Add a manual provenance check before reusing prompt text
Disable any auto-execution of ticket text as instructions
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels in the workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts itself touches no data classes and has no network egress, but Chatwoot handles customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and messages, and it has broad egress plus API integrations. If the pair shares a workspace or copied artifacts, customer data could leak into prompt content or external services. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports customer messages into files later consumed by awesome-prompts
IF shared storage or copy-paste moves customer data into prompt repositories
mitigations: Keep customer data out of prompt libraries
Review any exported transcripts before reuse
Separate workspaces for support data and prompt assets
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on exports to prompt tooling

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is marked runnable:false and has no write or network surfaces, while Chatwoot exposes integrations and broad egress. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface, so direct capability conflict is limited. The main risk is only if an external orchestrator gives both access to the same resource, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same workspace or API
IF Chatwoot integrations are configured to mutate resources also edited by prompt tooling
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per tool
Review integration scopes before enabling them

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply prompt text or examples that Chatwoot operators may reuse, and Chatwoot can act on customer-support workflows and integrations. If Chatwoot treats that content as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect replies or downstream actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Chatwoot agents or automations consume prompt-library text without review
IF generated support actions are triggered from unverified prompt content
mitigations: Require human review before sending support replies
Mark imported prompt text as non-authoritative
Log source provenance for reused prompts
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while awesome-prompts is a public prompt repository with no data-class handling. The pair creates a compliance risk if customer data is copied into prompt assets or external integrations, but the profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch directly. Medium fits the documented gap.
conditions: IF customer data is exported from Chatwoot into prompt repositories or third-party integrations
IF retention rules differ between support records and prompt artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated customer data out of prompt assets
Review retention settings for Chatwoot exports
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
